threads.title: Your claim LR-26-118077: our liability decision

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.subject: Your claim LR-26-118077: our liability decision
exchanges.body: Dear Mr. Benavides, we have finished our investigation of the October 9 accident at S 31st St and W Avenue H. Our insured, Wendell Fry, was turning left and should have yielded to you, and we accept that he is mostly responsible. The police report and an independent witness also put your speed well above the 35 mph limit as you entered on a yellow light, which contributed to the crash. We have assigned 70% of the responsibility to our insured and 30% to you. Under Texas law your damages are reduced by your share. Your damages are $9,318.00 (repairs $8,940.00 and rental, 9 days at $42.00, $378.00). We offer 70%, $6,522.60. If you have evidence we haven't seen, such as dash camera video or another witness, please send it and I'll review it. If you carry collision coverage, your own insurer may pay the remaining part of your repair, less your deductible. Maribel Ochoa, Leon River Mutual, 254-555-0180

threads.title: Your total loss settlement, claim LR-26-118170

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.subject: Your total loss settlement, claim LR-26-118170
exchanges.body: Dear Ms. Graves, I'm sorry about your Ranger. The repair estimate ($7,960) is more than the truck's value, so it is a total loss. The CCC valuation (attached) puts its actual cash value at $6,880 (base $7,020, condition -$140). Less your $500 collision deductible, the settlement is $6,380.00, payable to you (there is no lienholder). To accept, sign and mail the title and the enclosed power of attorney; we pay within 5 business days of acceptance, and we'll move the truck from Bell County Towing to Copart so you aren't charged storage. # Large loss report: LR-26-117730, Simmons v. Prewitt (committee 11/4)

Coverage: policy LRM-A-4410921 in force; BI 30/60; permissive driver = named insured. No coverage issues.
Liability: clear. Insured rear-ended claimant at a red light on the I-35 frontage road (8/14/2026); cited for following too closely.
Injuries: cervical strain; L4-5 disc herniation (MRI); ER; 14 weeks PT; orthopedic surgeon recommends epidural injections.
Specials: billed $21,850 (ER $6,420, MRI $3,980, spine consults $2,150, PT $9,300) + estimated injections $20,000 = $41,850; lost wages $4,600. Total economic $46,450 before general damages.
Liens: Baylor Scott & White hospital lien $3,210 (filed 9/28, Bell County).
Venue: Bell County district court; a verdict above $30,000 is likely given the herniation and recommended procedures.
Demand: $30,000 (limit) for a full release of the insured, expires Fri 11/6 5:00 p.m. CT.
Assessment: within limits; an ordinarily prudent insurer would accept given clear liability and damages well above the limit (Stowers).
Recommendation: accept and tender $30,000 by Thursday, with the hospital lien protected in the settlement (lienholder as joint payee or a lien release before funding).

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# LR-26-118077: liability analysis, 11/3

Evidence: CR-3 (Unit 1 Fry failed to yield turning left, cited; Unit 2 Benavides unsafe speed, est. 48 mph in a 35); independent witness Kowalczyk (recorded 11/3: claimant about 50 mph, did not slow, entered on yellow, said he was trying to make the light); insured's and claimant's statements (10/12, 10/13); scene diagram (Enclave past the centerline at impact).
Analysis: a left-turning driver must yield to oncoming traffic, so the insured bears the larger share. The claimant's speed, about 13-15 mph over the limit on a yellow, contributed.
Decision: insured 70%, claimant 30%. The claimant is not more than 50% responsible, so his damages are reduced by 30% (Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code 33.001, 33.012).
Damages: repair $8,940.00 + rental 9 days x $42.00 = $378.00, total $9,318.00. Offer 70% = $6,522.60. Within my authority.
Next: liability letter to the claimant and the insured today; reserve $9,318 reduced to $6,522.60.
